expectations.text: Signup shows a pending state while submitting and a success confirmation afterwards
expectations.evidence: index.html: on submit, setPending(true) (L879 -> L852-867) locks the button width (L856), sets aria-busy='true' on the button (L857), changes the label to 'Joining…' (L858), prepends a spinning .spinner (L859-860; CSS L143-147, with a reduced-motion fallback at L445) and makes the input readOnly (L854). 'if (pending) return; // ignore double presses' (L871) is the double-submit guard. After the simulated api.join resolves (1.1 s, L786-793), markJoined (L928-932) -> showSuccess (L898-913) replaces the form with the template 'You’re on the list!' / 'We’ll email <email> as soon as your invite is ready.' (L679-695) and focuses the title (tabindex=-1, L911). The success is persisted to storage, so it survives a reload (L882, L962-966). The failure path restores the button and shows an inline message (L885-889). Screenshots confirm both states: scratch/flow-desktop-pending.png (spinner + 'Joining…') and scratch/flow-desktop-success.png. Minor: the button is not disabled (by design), and there is no live-region announcement of 'Joining…'. The success title gets focus instead.

expectations.text: Final response explains key UX decisions (ideally citing the laws)
expectations.evidence: RESPONSE.md has a dedicated '## UX decisions' section (L7-15) with 8 bullets. Each pairs a decision with its reason and cites a law: one primary CTA style (§L28 Von Restorff, §L10 Hick); a thumb-reachable sticky mobile CTA that hides when the keyboard is open (§L07 Fitts); a forgiving email field with typo suggestions (§L24 Postel); errors only on submit and a never-disabled button (§L20, §L29); immediate feedback with a fixed-width spinner and the double-press guard (§L06 Doherty); a designed success ending (§L23 Peak-End); an interactive sample week (§L17 Mental Model); and a conventional layout (§L11 Jakob). It also has 'Where I deliberately broke a rule' (L17, §L19 Occam) and a 'Before you launch' list of honest caveats (L30-35: simulated API, placeholder content, privacy link, no invented testimonials). Small nit: some citations are bare codes (e.g. '§L20, §L29' on L11), which a non-specialist can't decode.

notes: Iteration 2 = SKILL.md changes: proportionate verification (scan, fix, re-scan once), case file folded into the hand-off when fixing, scanners treated as evidence, pointer-based target sizing. Baselines reused from iteration 1 (same condition).
Quality held: with_skill 37/37 (100%) vs baseline 33/37 (89%); scanner scores 98-100 vs 89-94.
Cost dropped vs iteration 1: time 1384s -> 1131s (-18%), tokens 274K -> 240K (-12%). Remaining overhead vs baseline: +355s, +100K tokens, spent on flow tests that caught real bugs in every run.
New statute observed in practice: nav run sized sidebar rows 44px on touch and 36px only under (pointer: fine); baseline shipped 36px icon-only rows to tablets.
Blind comparison (eval 3) again prefers with_skill; baseline has an SSR hydration mismatch (localStorage read during render).
Remaining weaknesses found by the grader (addressed after this run): long CHANGES.md despite 'short' request; 'Dashboard' tab label truncated at 360px.
Manual assertions remain non-discriminating (both configs pass); discriminating signals are scanner checks, law-cited reasoning and blind qualitative comparison.
